resources.string: Talk on your iPhone

Hear calls and talk with your iPhone’s own microphone and speaker. Android keeps call audio away from apps, so Pairline starts a small helper through Wireless debugging, a switch in Developer options that you turn on. No extra app and no root. Both phones also need to be on the same Wi-Fi.

Good to know
After a restart
Android turns Wireless debugging off when the phone restarts or leaves Wi-Fi. Pairline turns it back on by itself as soon as this phone is on Wi-Fi, and starts its helper.
Using this phone’s hotspot

Wireless debugging works only while this phone is on a Wi-Fi network, so turning on its hotspot (or Wi-Fi off) turns it off. Start Pairline’s helper on Wi-Fi first: it keeps running after you switch to the hotspot, until the phone restarts.
Banking apps
Some banking apps won’t open while Developer options or Wireless debugging are on. Pairline turns them back on whenever its helper needs them, so turn Talk on iPhone off while you use such an app.
Forget pairing
Stops the helper and deletes Pairline’s key. Also remove “Pairline” under Wireless debugging › Paired devices.
Forget the pairing?
Talk on iPhone stops until you pair Pairline with Wireless debugging again. Calls still ring on the iPhone, but their audio stays on this phone.
Call audio goes over your Wi-Fi, encrypted end to end. It’s never recorded or stored.

Talk on iPhone
What does Wireless debugging do here? Does it need root?

Android lets only its own debugging tool reach call audio. With Wireless debugging on, Pairline starts a small helper with that tool’s rights, from its own app: no extra app and no root. The helper only carries call audio and handles the call keypad, mute and speaker. It stops when the phone restarts, and “Forget pairing” removes Pairline’s access for good.
Why does call audio go back to this phone after a restart?

Android turns Wireless debugging off every time the phone restarts or leaves Wi-Fi, and the helper stops with it. Pairline turns Wireless debugging back on by itself as soon as this phone is on a Wi-Fi network, and starts its helper again. Until then calls still ring and work on the iPhone, with the audio on this phone.
An app complains that debugging is on

Some banking and payment apps refuse to open while Developer options or Wireless debugging are on. While Talk on iPhone is on, Pairline turns them back on whenever its helper needs them. Turn Talk on iPhone off while you use such an app.
I hear calls on the iPhone, but they can’t hear me

Some phones don’t let any app feed audio into a call. Then you hear calls on the iPhone and talk on this phone. After each call the iPhone asks how it sounded; your answers help Pairline try another way on the next call.

Root mode

For rooted phones only. Talk on iPhone’s helper starts through your root app (Magisk, KernelSU…) instead of Wireless debugging: no Developer options, and it keeps working after a restart, even without Wi-Fi. It runs with the same limited rights as before, not as root. Your root app asks once.
Restart Bluetooth when stuck

Sometimes Android’s Bluetooth stops working until it’s turned off and on. With this on and Talk on iPhone’s helper running, Pairline does that by itself when Bluetooth keeps failing while the iPhone isn’t connected, at most once an hour. Bluetooth headphones or a watch reconnect after a few seconds.
